x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: States' capital outlay rose from 2.17% of GDP in FY22 to 2.37% in FY25 (Economic Survey 2025-26). Statement 3 is false: excluding SASCI, capital outlay fell from 2.11% to 1.92% over the same period, it did not rise.

All three are correct: under Article 293 a State owing money to the Centre needs the Centre's consent to borrow; since 2005-06 external loans reach States only through the Centre; and for general category States they are passed on back-to-back. So D.

All three are correct: the differential is r − g (effective interest rate minus nominal GDP growth); when g exceeds r the debt-GDP ratio can fall even with a small primary deficit, and when r exceeds g a primary surplus is needed. So D.

All three are correct: the FRBM Act as amended in 2018 set general government debt at 60% with the Centre at 40% by 2024-25, and the N.K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended 60% by 2023, split as Centre 40% and States 20%. So D.

All four are non-marketable internal debt of the Centre: saving and compensation bonds, 14-day Intermediate T-Bills issued to States, special securities issued to the NSSF and securities issued to international financial institutions (IMF, World Bank, ADB). Market loans, T-Bills and Cash Management Bills are the marketable part. So D.
